messages:
sofia: quick q — how should runtime handle 429s across per-route vs global quotas? specifically: Retry-After semantics (seconds vs http-date), headers to expose, and whether we should auto-fallback to cheaper models or just return 429. also curious about KV-cache hot paths and burst behavior.

mike: short: return 429 immediately when quota is exceeded. include Retry-After in seconds (primary), and keep old http-date support for backcompat. also surface per-route scope in headers so SDKs can make smarter choices.

dinesh: runtime note: we treat quota as token-bucket (refill + burst). when bucket empty -> immediate 429. we could enqueue short-lived requests but that complicates SLOs. recommend explicit fallback config instead of implicit queuing.

lisa: product: +1 on seconds. older clients sometimes expect HTTP-date, so we should parse both. for UX, if customers want auto-fallback to cheaper model, make that a per-tenant flag. default behavior = 429.

mike: example headers proposal:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 15
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1805550015
X-RateLimit-Scope: route:/v1/generate
X-RateLimit-Burst: 150
```
(Reset is epoch seconds; Retry-After is seconds to wait)

dinesh: also include an adjusted header for cache-aware counts: e.g. X-RateLimit-Adjusted-Remaining to show remaining credits after accounting for cache-hit discounts. helps debuggability on hot paths.

sofia: body shape? do we prefer a small JSON error with machine-friendly fields?

mike: yes. propose: 
```json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 15,
  "scope": "route:/v1/generate",
  "reason": "per_route_quota"
}
```
SDKs should read Retry-After header, then fallback to this body if header missing.

lisa: about SDK behavior: default = no automatic retry for non-idempotent calls. for generate endpoints we should only auto-retry if caller explicitly opts-in (e.g., retry_policy: "safe_retry"), and always respect Retry-After (and do exponential backoff + jitter). document patterns in devdocs.

dinesh: KV-cache nuance: when a request hits cache and we serve from KV, we should decrement a cheaper cost (or not decrement) depending on config. We need to expose which requests were cache hits in observability but not in the 429 itself. header suggestion: X-Cache-Hit: true/false. and X-RateLimit-Adjusted-Remaining if we apply discounts.

sofia: backcompat question: existing clients expect X-RateLimit-Reset in seconds. any breaking change risks?

mike: keep X-RateLimit-Reset (epoch) and add Retry-After (seconds). do not remove anything for now. deprecate via doc notes and telemetry.

lisa: fallback behavior decision: allow per-route config with these options: ["return_429", "fallback_to_model:<id>", "enqueue_short_window:<secs>"]. default = return_429. Product will add flag in console.

mike: runtime action: add support for these headers and the cache-adjusted remaining counter. ensure we never return both Retry-After and a misleading X-RateLimit-Remaining (0 but immediate refill). test cases: burst exhaustion, sustained overage, cache-heavy traffic.

dinesh: implement token-bucket parameters in config: refill_rate (tokens/sec), burst_capacity, cooldown_window (secs). we will emit X-RateLimit-Burst and X-RateLimit-Reset to help clients.

deploy-bot: rate-limiter/v2 pushed to staging at 1805550200 :rocket:

sofia: ok action items: mike -> add headers + body shape + tests (ETA 2 days), dinesh -> KV-cache adjusted counters + X-Cache-Hit (ETA 3 days), lisa -> console flag + SDK guidance update (ETA 4 days). I'll create a follow-up ticket and sync. :thumbsup:

mike: ack :thumbsup:

dinesh: ack :eyes:

lisa: thanks, will add to roadmap.
